items.title: Fake medicines worth Rs 5 crore seized near Bidadi; 4 arrested, SIT probe likely
items.summary: The Karnataka Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) Department has busted a counterfeit medicine racket operating from an unlicensed unit near Bidadi in Ramanagara district, with officials seizing spurious medicines, packaging material and drug-filling equipment worth nearly Rs 5 crore, according to The Hindu . The raid was conducted by the FSDA’s Drug Enforcement Wing and police at a farmhouse in Kurubara Karenahalli, near the Bidadi toll gate, following a tip-off about the alleged manufacture, repackaging and relabelling of medicines. According to officials, medicines procured from manufacturing units in Himachal Pradesh and Telangana were allegedly being repackaged and labelled to make them appear to be products of prominent multinational pharmaceutical companies. The relabelled medicines were then allegedly sold at substantially higher prices. The bench will comprise Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana . The matter was earlier being heard by a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and NK Singh. items.summary: Delhi based criminal trial lawyer Vijay Aggarwal , who represents fugitive businessman Mehul Choksi, has been arrested and charged in London on four counts of sexual assault involving two women, Times of India reported . Aggarwal’s personal assistant, Manpreet Kaur, has also been charged with two counts of intentionally encouraging or assisting the commission of sexual assault offences. Aggarwal (57) and Kaur (41) appeared before Westminster Magistrates’ Court on August 13. Both were remanded to custody and their case was sent to Southwark Crown Court, where a plea and trial preparation hearing is scheduled for September 10. The two Indian nationals were arrested on August 11 at a serviced townhouse on Brick Street in Mayfair, where they were reportedly staying. The arrests followed complaints of sexual assault at the property. Three of the charges against Aggarwal relate to alleged incidents involving a woman on August 9. He is accused of intentionally touching her in a sexual manner without her consent, an offence under Section 3 of the Sexual Offences Act, 2003. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday directed the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to examine all six allegations flagged by the Enforcement Directorate (ED) against Indiabulls Housing Finance and related entities. A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant , Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana recorded that the five out of six allegations in the ED complaint had been investigated by the Delhi Police Economic Offences Wing (EOW), which had opined that further investigation was not advisable. The Court noted that the CBI was seeking further investigation into the sixth allegation. Subsequently, it directed the special judge in Mumbai to decide the CBI's application for further investigation within two weeks of August 24. "The CBI shall thereafter submit a progress/status report to the Supreme Court," directed the Court. items.title: Telangana: Two class 10 students held for murder of their school principal
items.summary: Two 16-year-old boys studying in class 10 were held by the Telangana police in the murder case of their school principal, Roopa Reddy, in Nalgonda district. Roopa, principal of the Nagarjuna Grammar Concept School, was found stabbed to death in her house in Kondamallepally on August 11. Over a week of investigation later, Nalgonda Superintendent of Police (SP) Sharat Chandra Pawar announced on Wednesday, August 19 that two students of the school were allegedly involved in the murder. Around the time of her death on the evening of August 11, Roopa was talking to her aunt and said the word ‘babu’ just before the phone was switched off, the police found during interrogations. The SP said that while they were looking at family members and persons with crime records as suspects, they also wondered whom she might have addressed as ‘babu’ and speculated if it could be one of her students. When the school reopened on August 17 after a break for mourning, the police looked for any students who missed classes or behaved in a suspicious way, the SP said. items.title: Kerala HC stays suspension of Kasaragod teacher over Savarkar quiz question
items.summary: The Kerala High Court stayed the suspension of a school teacher from Kasaragod who was suspended after a quiz question identified VD Savarkar as the freedom fighter who received the “maximum punishment” from the British. The suspension has been kept in abeyance for a month. Justice Viju Abraham passed the interim order on Wednesday, August 19, while hearing a petition filed by K Guruprasad Rai, a teacher at AUP School Pallathadukka. The court, however, permitted the disciplinary proceedings initiated against him to continue. “I'm inclined to pass an interim order staying the operation of...order of suspension for a period of one month. But I'm permitting the disciplinary proceedings to continue,” the order said. The controversy began after an inter-school Social Science Club Freedom Quiz held in Kasaragod on August 6. One of the questions asked which freedom fighter had received the maximum punishment from the British, with VD Savarkar given as the answer. Rai questioned the legality of the suspension and the disciplinary proceedings initiated following an inquiry by the education authorities. items.title: Kerala High Court bats for full-fledged lab at Pamba to test quality of food served at Sabarimala
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently said that it was high time that a full-fledged food testing laboratory was established at Pamba to ensure prompt quality checks of Aravana, Appam (sacred food offerings) and other food items supplied at the Sabarimala temple [ Dr Mahendra Kumar PS v The State of Kerala & ors and connected case ]. A Division Bench of Justice Raja Vijayaraghavan V and Justice KV Jayakumar took note of concerns that the existing food testing laboratory at Pamba was not equipped to conduct a detailed and continuous testing of such food items. The Court was told that samples of food items had to be transported to laboratories at Pathanamthitta or Thiruvananthapuram for analysis. The Court observed that such an arrangement was not enough to ensure fast and effective quality control of the food items at Sabarimala. " We are of the considered view that it is high time that a fully fledged and comprehensive food testing laboratory is established at Pamba itself, so that the requisite tests can be conducted there without delay, thereby ensuring strict compliance with food safety standards, " the Court added. items.title: GHAC Arbitration Week 2026 to bring together four SC judges, former judges, leading arbitration practitioners, others
items.summary: The Gujarat High Court Arbitration Centre (GHAC) is set to host GHAC Arbitration Week 2026 from September 3 to 6, 2026. The theme for the Arbitration Week is "Three stakeholders, three days, one vision" and is centred around building Gujarat's institutional arbitration ecosystem. The four-day programme will bring together judges, senior advocates, government law officers and international arbitration practitioners for discussions on developments in domestic and international arbitration. The opening ceremony will be held on September 3, while the substantive sessions of the arbitration week will take place from September 4 to 6. The programme will feature keynote addresses, panel discussions and sessions on the evolution of India's arbitration regime and its engagement with international arbitration. The conference examines a variety of themes. Not only does it reflect on how the law has moved forward since 2015, but it also looks at amendments required for a healthier arbitration regime. Moreover, it includes contemporary themes such as the use of Artificial Intelligence in Arbitration and conflict of law issues that arise in international arbitration. Guests: Bhupendrabhai Patel
